comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C36-C46, C82 regarding GENIUS performance across six prediction tasks. Both evaluations find the comparative results well-supported, with peer reviewer explicitly endorsing the finding that spatial representation and 3D contacts lead to best performance.

Complete agreement on claims C83, C124 regarding limitations and future directions. Both evaluations accept the acknowledgment that finer-grained spatial organization (TADs) could be explored and that the current work is proof-of-concept.

Strong alignment on claims C76-C81 regarding mixed validation results in early-stage disease. Both evaluations appreciate the honest reporting of negative results and accept the statistical analysis and interpretation without challenge.

High concordance on claims C6-C8, C30, C32-C35, C93-C94 describing GENIUS framework and code availability. Both find the core methodology valuable and well-described. OpenEval includes C95 (implementation details) not explicitly mentioned in peer review. Peer review includes C85 (novelty claim) which OpenEval evaluates separately as UNCERTAIN.

Strong agreement on claims C69-C75, C87 regarding validation methodology and statistical testing. Both evaluations accept the permutation analysis and validation approach. OpenEval additionally covers C31, C88, C105-C106 (validation cohort details) not explicitly addressed in peer review.

Partial overlap on attribution analysis claims C51-C57. Peer review R3 accepts these findings as part of broader cancer application validation. OpenEval provides more detailed evaluation of the chromosomal location patterns and mutation vs. expression/methylation observations.

Partial overlap on gene identification claims C58, C60-C62. Both evaluations support the novel gene discoveries. Peer review R3 also covers C10-C11, C50-C57 (broader cancer application context), while OpenEval R5 focuses specifically on C58-C68 (gene identification and validation against COSMIC).

Partial overlap on methodological motivation claims C4-C5, C15. OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN due to difficulty verifying 'first' claim and speculative nature of multiple testing critique. Peer review R8 finds the methodological motivations SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting the critique of traditional methods. Peer R8 also covers C13, C17, C21 not in OpenEval R14.

Minor overlap on code availability claims C93-C94. OpenEval R1 finds availability explicitly stated and supports the claim. Peer R7 rates as UNCERTAIN, raising significant concerns about practical usability (hard-coded paths, lack of error handling) despite confirming availability.

Minimal overlap on claim C50 (validation performance). OpenEval R3 focuses on dataset composition and processing methods (C29, C49-C50, C97-C104). Peer R3 addresses broader cancer application validation including metastatic prediction and gene identification (C10-C11, C50-C62).

Partial overlap on background claims C13, C15, C17 regarding genomics challenges. OpenEval R12 evaluates these as SUPPORTED background claims (C1-C3, C12-C17). Peer R8 accepts these as valid methodological motivations for GENIUS along with C4-C5, C21.

Minimal overlap on novelty claim C85. OpenEval R14 rates C85 as UNCERTAIN due to difficulty verifying 'first' claim. Peer R1 includes C85 in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of GENIUS framework as 'new approach,' without specifically scrutinizing the 'first' assertion.

OpenEval R8 evaluates UMAP visualization findings (C47-C48, C84, C117) as SUPPORTED with appropriate negative controls. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific visualization claims.

OpenEval R9 evaluates data transformation criteria (C107-C112) as SUPPORTED with clear mathematical definitions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific preprocessing details.

OpenEval R10 evaluates training details and computational accessibility (C96, C113-C116, C122-C123) as SUPPORTED, though notes 'most modern laptops' claim may be optimistic. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these implementation details.

OpenEval R11 evaluates Integrated Gradients method description (C118-C121) as SUPPORTED with appropriate technical detail. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific interpretability method claims.

OpenEval R13 evaluates deep learning background and interpretation methods (C18-C28) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer R8 includes only C21 from this set as part of broader methodological motivation evaluation.

OpenEval R15 evaluates biological interpretation of PCAT6 findings (C89-C92) as UNCERTAIN, noting tumor suppressor hypothesis is speculative and requires experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific biological interpretations.
